purpose: PREREG_CP0_2026-08-28.md section 2.2 acceptance test P1-e. The three candidate definitions of channel 1 all pass P1-a and P1-b, so this file registers a synthetic workload on which they DISAGREE ARITHMETICALLY, together with the hand-computed value of each. Written BEFORE any measurement; the checker only compares.

definitions_under_test.D1_n_requests_chunked: distinct rids truncated at least once (the registered counter, prereg 2.1)
definitions_under_test.D2_n_chunk_events: number of truncations (the registered counter, prereg 2.1); admission + continuation
definitions_under_test.D3_n_prompts_longer_than_cps: prompts whose own length exceeds chunked_prefill_size -- NOT channel 1, it is the offline lower bound computed by measure_served_population.py. If the instrument is secretly measuring this, the phases below kill it.

engine_assumptions.max_prefill_tokens: large enough that rem_input_tokens never binds
engine_assumptions.kv_pool: large enough that rem_total_tokens / cur_rem_tokens never bind

phases.name: sequential
phases.note: One request at a time, each awaited to completion before the next is sent. The batch budget is therefore reset for every request and the split of each request depends only on its own length -- which makes every number below hand-derivable and makes the phase exact on GPU as well as on CPU.
hand_derivation: L=1500, cps=512: forward 1 truncates to 512 (admission, M1/M2); prefix=512, remaining 988 > 512 so forward 2 truncates again to 512 (continuation, M3); prefix=1024, remaining 476 <= 512 so forward 3 is the last chunk and is NOT an event. chunks=3, events=2.
L=512: 512 <= rem_chunk_tokens 512, the non-chunked branch is taken (the comparison is <=, not <). chunks=1, events=0.
L=513: forward 1 truncates to 512 (admission); remaining 1 <= 512 so forward 2 is the last chunk. chunks=2, events=1.

phases.name: backlog
phases.note: Eight prompts of 200 tokens each -- every one SHORTER than cps, so D3 = 0 by construction while D1 > 0. This is the phase that kills a length-based instrument. The exact numbers hold only when all eight are already in the waiting queue when the first prefill batch is formed; on GPU that is a race, so the GPU assertions below are inequalities and only the CPU loop is checked exactly.
hand_derivation: batch 1: budget 512 -> r1 200 (rem 312), r2 200 (rem 112), r3 200 > 112 so truncate to 112 (event, admission); rem 0 -> budget_state OTHER, loop breaks. extend = 200+200+112 = 512.

batch 2: r3 continues with 88 remaining, 88 <= 512 so NOT an event (rem 424); r4 200 (rem 224), r5 200 (rem 24), r6 200 > 24 truncate to 24 (event, admission); rem 0 breaks. extend = 88+200+200+24 = 512.
batch 3: r6 continues with 176 remaining, not an event (rem 336); r7 200 (rem 136), r8 200 > 136 truncate to 136 (event, admission); rem 0 breaks. extend = 176+200+136 = 512.
batch 4: r8 continues with 64 remaining, not an event. extend = 64.
D1 = |{r3, r6, r8}| = 3. D2 = 3 (all admission; no request is truncated twice because every remainder is <= 512). D3 = 0. Total tokens 3*512 + 64 = 1600 = 8*200.

gpu_assertions.why: D3 = 0 is exact by construction (no prompt exceeds 512), so any nonzero D1 here is a separation from D3 no matter how the burst races.

separation_claim.statement: In one boot at cps 512 the three candidate definitions take three pairwise different values (5, 6, 2). An instrument that reports any one of them cannot be mistaken for an instrument that reports another.

p1d_positive_control.prompt_lens_note: 16 concurrent prompts of about 341 tokens (the mean of the served ShareGPT population, served_population.json prompt_len.mean = 341.4). 16 * 341 = 5456 > 4096, so a fully backlogged first batch must exhaust the budget at least once.
p1d_positive_control.why: prereg 2.2 P1-d. Without this a 'count prompts longer than cps' instrument scores full marks on P1-a and P1-b.
